groups.title: Design generation-aware reload, IPC and drain ownership
groups.reason: The A4 primary-precreation/lookup, namespace-recycling, own-slot and epoch-liveness cases are adapted. NR-19 adapts only the generation-ring ownership helper through stable original-DPDK ring names and resident-authenticated pidfd ownership; it does not claim production packet dispatch or external TCP/UDP. TC-3 adapts only the named same-generation two-masters/single-consumer observer scenario. TC-5 adapts only the live coordinate-query/ring-name selection scenario using Ker's authenticated typed control request; it does not implement FF_RELOAD_CMD_QUERY or ff_ipc ABI. Optional ring-PMD bursts and live standby/reclaim tests retain their documented bounded scopes. Production generation-aware packet dispatch/flow-map and cross-generation flow drain remain unqualified. The paired TC-3 profile proves only that its selected exception endpoint and fixed packet queues share the resident-authenticated owner key; it does not establish full F-Stack exception/KNI behavior. Physical PMD handover, queued-packet crash matrix, general hardware-driver packet journals, graceful handover and full reload remain unqualified. Registration/control probes do not satisfy the remaining complete source generation contracts. TC-7 adapts only `test_it_a14_usr2_drain_peer_semantics` through authenticated drain authorization and worker-origin freshness, peer selection/fallback, and exact cleanup; it does not claim drain-TX, external TX, flow-map, TCP continuity, or full reload. The P1 directory cases missing, invalid, full, primary_slot_busy and success are scenario-adapted. Success covers the real default-off and generation-rings-enabled directory behavior in separate EAL namespaces, plus production attach replay for all eight ring pointers; it does not claim a literal graceful_reload switch or F-Stack ABI equivalence. live_slot remains blocked because Ker selects any free slot. P1 now additionally adapts only test_p1_drain_queue_ownership and test_p1_drain_peer_tx: the real EAL fixture proves the no-peer +2 and foreign-peer +1 configured-RX cleanup policies, retains the other six ring objects, checks exact replay/idempotence and same-ring re-admission, and restores the 511-object pool. The held-operation fatal case is a fail-closed safety check, not broader packet/TX or reload coverage. Nonowner TX, foreign-epoch TX, flow-map, external TX and full reload remain under this issue. Since this earlier scope note, test_p1_drain_nonowner_tx has been adapted only for the authenticated same-master/epoch mode where a live generation-1 PMD/RX owner coexists with generation-0 detach; the actual EAL evidence proves RX q0/g0 +1 reclamation, retention of TX q1/g0 and six other ring objects, exact owner-snapshot rejection/replay denial, same-ring re-admission, and final pool 511. This does not qualify TX burst or payload behavior. Foreign-epoch TX, flow-map, external TX and full reload remain tracked here. P1 additionally adapts only test_p1_drain_empty_qconf through the real EAL empty-cleanup-mask test: it retains all eight populated ring objects and restores the pool, while the invalid-selected-entry failure remains safety evidence only. The pinned `test_f_m4_1_drain_ring_full_visible` is now scenario-adapted only for actual TX ring-full visibility: one real enqueue-full event, caller ownership of the rejected object, FIFO drain/cleanup, and typed counters `tx_full=1`, `tx_drop=0`, `tx_peak=64` at capacity 64, `rx_peak=0`. The full 14-suite guest and event-peak negative control are bound in `tests/fstack-provenance.json`; no physical NIC, external TX, payload/flow behavior or full reload is claimed.  RX-15 orphan cleanup now has partial primary-component evidence for exact pidfd liveness/identity rejection, selective queued RX/TX reclamation, live-consumer FIFO preservation and final consumer death. Its no-directory/not-yet-attached, purge-lock/reset-timeout, dead-marker/fresh-unregistered-packet and full slot-reset branches remain incomplete; the source case stays in this issue. Live-consumer in-flight RX/TX leases now have bounded reap-timeout/gate-rollback and staged-return recovery evidence in three primary-component profiles. Those active-operation leases do not qualify the source external purge-owner lock/reset timeout; RX-15 remains partial under this issue. UT-NR-14 now has partial real-resident control-frame evidence for typed query roundtrips, malformed record/header/field rejection and cached/id-conflicting sequence handling, with no leased-object or slot leak. F-Stack reload subcommand meanings, fill/parse ABI and NULL/optional-output contracts remain incomplete; the case stays in this issue. P2 release-epoch proof now has partial real-resident control-reservation evidence: live or socket-disconnected direct children block RELEASE; exact pidfd deaths reclaim individual mbufs, and the final borrower death permits release. Secondary EAL/hardware entry, STOPPED proof, bounded reclaim/refusal counters and RX-owner-generation transfer remain incomplete. The source case stays in this issue. P2 hardware-user proof now has partial pre-EAL registration/census evidence: exact RESERVE sequence replay retains one lease, duplicate coordinates and malformed credentials/bounds preserve the census, and valid successor registration succeeds. This is not hardware-user ACTIVE/STOPPED state, independent user_add operation idempotence or users_clear/epoch_users_clear; those source contracts remain tracked here. P2 orphan epoch lifetime now has partial real-resident control-reservation evidence after exact master death, including EOF-disconnected/frozen borrowers and staged two-coordinate recovery. This is exact pidfd-based lifetime, not fresh/stale heartbeat takeover or hardware RX ownership; those source contracts remain incomplete. M5 cross-master naming now has partial evidence from all128 production-format names and original DPDK ring creation/lookup, duplicate rejection, independent64-token FIFOs and selective slot-ring recreation. F-Stack high process IDs, message-type families and legacy/literal name ABI remain incomplete; primary-only token tests are not secondary-EAL/mbuf/epoch-admission evidence. The twelve test_ff_ipc.c address/ownership cases are now adapted separately through exported ker::ipc with unchanged pinned transport and real primary/20-secondary shared-ring evidence. This optional caller-owned component does not complete the remaining resident generation/reload contracts. M5 epoch-slot/ring-name and graceful-zero naming invariance are now adapted through the provider-side exported IPC builder and real unsuffixed secondary transport. Arbitration and hardware/data-plane handover remain separate incomplete cases. The separate optional ker::reload component now completes UT-NR-14 original message fill/parse serialization through unchanged source and real primary/secondary transport. Existing resident-envelope evidence remains separate; this adds no execution of FreeBSD control commands, directory arbitration or full reload. UT-NR-26 ownership markers and UT-NR-11 park barrier are now separately qualified through exported same-master synchronous poll gating, original helpers and actual net_ring primary/secondary RX/TX, including a held callback, exact park-epoch proof, reverse transfer and installed-consumer repetition. This does not complete directory/user-proof/cross-master/TCP/full reload contracts.
acceptance: Specify generation lifecycle, single-consumer admission, peer liveness, failure recovery and ownership before adding implementation.
Implement only runtime/device/ownership adapters around original Linux, with actual multiprocess data and teardown evidence.
Qualify each listed case, including delayed/foreign epochs, bounded growth, overflow, purge and the external reload acceptance flow; do not substitute a same-process FIFO.

groups.title: Define a supported host exception bridge and KNI policy adaptation
groups.reason: Actual original-DPDK classification, host/native Linux service routing, console/general admission and invalid-process rejection now also have real per-port RX lcore ownership. Original EAL main membership in the port list is accepted/rejected before app entry as required by the two source fixtures; both selected cores genuinely poll disjoint PMD queues and preserve owned handoff/cleanup. Six remaining source contracts use future-generation/non-owner/inject-ring or named statistics/slot allocation state and are not proved by same-generation EAL lcores. Static port ownership still lacks fragment reassembly/flow ownership, deeper/opaque encapsulations, full multicast/generation fanout and automatic cross-stack ephemeral discovery; explicit fragment drops are not migration completion.
acceptance: Choose an actual supported DPDK/Linux exception device and explicit packet ownership boundary; do not add successful no-op KNI stubs.
Verify RX/TX, partial acceptance, full queues, rate limits, malformed frames, IPv4/IPv6 classification and cleanup through real adapter paths.
Keep protocol decisions in original Linux; do not copy a simplified F-Stack/FreeBSD protocol parser as a replacement stack.

Resolve fragment/encapsulation and automatic local-port ownership with original Linux facilities, or keep an explicit unsupported boundary. Do not build Ker-owned reassembly or connection tracking merely to steer packets.

groups.title: Qualify RSS steering and queue-aware source-port contracts
groups.reason: Exact source audit distinguishes configuration/table/guard assertions, standalone real-DPDK software equivalence, skipped unready microbench and actual RSS packet landing. Ker key/RETA control readback and independent vhost queue injection do not implement the original FreeBSD PCB caller source-port candidate-table integration. Original Linux allocation remains authoritative; see docs/fstack-rss-contracts.md.
acceptance: Qualify exact source assertions in docs/fstack-rss-contracts.md through actual Ker consumers, distinguishing early unready guards, software arithmetic and ready-context behavior; do not require a physical NIC merely for a pure helper assertion or label a skipped microbench a performance pass.

Identify an original Linux allocation extension point with real routing/conflict/range/fallback semantics before source-port steering. Preserve automatic original Linux port allocation; do not implement a Ker-owned TCP source-port/state machine or add an unused optimization API.

Separately prove real IPv4/IPv6 RSS packet landing with an appropriate original PMD/input profile, actual hash/queue observations and independent computation from queried key/algorithm/RETA. Key/RETA control readback and deliberately alternating backend queues are insufficient.

Qualify table lifecycle/hit/miss/caller-owned rotation, enabled/disabled/degraded states and ready-context recheck/range paths; record actual non-skipped performance evidence before any microbench claim.

groups.title: Define packet-dispatch and PCB callback adaptation boundaries
groups.reason: F-Stack dispatcher/context and PCB-local-address callbacks are not Ker APIs. A Linux packet-device bridge or legacy dispatcher is not a registration-compatible substitute.
acceptance: For every callback, decide whether a runtime hook has a useful Ker caller and an ownership/quiescence contract, or document why the FreeBSD ABI is excluded.
If supported, exercise registration, context forwarding, replacement/unregistration and packet delivery through the actual adapter.
Do not expose an unused setter solely to pass smoke tests or bypass original Linux protocol behavior.

groups.title: Resolve device/run lifecycle and upstream fault-injection contracts
groups.reason: Actual native context allocation/free/fd ownership and both-NULL TX/RX rejection are now qualified, including real Linux registration/removal and traffic. The bounded late interface activation failure/no-app cleanup case and callback-stop-return-teardown smoke case are also scenario-adapted; neither claims the F-Stack ABI, exit(1), multi-port rollback, or coupled EAL-lcore main-loop implementation. Remaining cases require owned FreeBSD mbuf/m_copydata disposal semantics or that unimplemented coupled-loop architecture; borrowed iovecs must never be freed as an mbuf substitute.
acceptance: Separate portable startup/ownership requirements from FreeBSD ABI/callback/ordering requirements for each listed case.
Implement missing supported adapters with real registration/run/stop/failure and cleanup evidence, or record an explicit incompatible boundary.
Do not treat real Linux failure tests as proof of F-Stack callback forwarding or an injected m_copydata failure.

groups.title: Adapt typed vdev, bond and multi-port configuration
groups.reason: Three typed interface/vdev/bond configuration allocation-failure rejection scenarios now have real loader/CLI failure and recovery evidence. Remaining source fixture/ABI, combined topology and RSS/lcore contracts stay partial; real typed device traffic does not prove those remaining assertions. The exact repeated source bond sequence now drives original mode4 PMD readback for final members0/1, primary1,MACcc:dd:ee:ff:00:11,l34 and independent Linux LACP/dual-stack ICMP after member-path loss. Source member names are explicitly translated to the two TAP ethdev IDs; combined bond/vdev and allocator ABI remain incomplete.
acceptance: Specify useful typed configuration mappings to real supported EAL/PMD options while preserving strict validation.
Test repeated sections/options, missing count/configuration, invalid section/index and allocation failures before runtime side effects.
Qualify actual vdev/bond/multi-port behavior and cleanup on a capable backend; configuration parsing alone is not a device pass.

Resolve the pinned source iface+Unix-socket mismatch explicitly. Retain qualified named vhost-kernel iface traffic/rollback coverage; do not drop iface or call socket-backend traffic a full source fixture pass.

groups.title: Resolve remaining typed configuration and intentional schema differences
groups.reason: Ker typed settings and Linux defaults differ from F-Stack global structures, permissive handlers, FreeBSD boot fields and several fixture/default/ignore contracts. Existing subset coverage must not be promoted to complete fixture equivalence. VLAN configuration-record list allocation rejection now qualifies through the production loader. RX core-list allocation failure evidence does not qualify the remaining global F-Stack proc_lcore allocation contract. The explicit disabled-jumbo MTU policy is now adapted separately by native-fstack-mtu-enable-config/live; it no longer remains in this group. The source no-options startup failure (misnamed empty_ini) is now separately adapted by native-fstack-config-lifecycle; valid Ker CLI-only configuration remains supported. Malformed VLAN section failure is now adapted through the actual Ker typed reader/CLI; permissive orphan/filter and out-of-array skip contracts remain in this group. Malformed port-section rejection is now separately adapted through the production named-interface reader and CLI with no worker/application execution; numeric-port ABI and over-max skipping remain incomplete. The exact dpdk_extra_keys bond timing tuple poll100/up200/down300 now has original-PMD initial/final readback and independent host/native Linux LACP, dual-stack ICMP and member-path-loss evidence. This removes the unqualified down_delay300 sub-gap, not the remaining allow/port_list, vdev tuple, complete config ABI, physical NIC or exact failover-latency contracts.
acceptance: Review each source assertion and identify a supported typed/runtime adaptation or an explicitly unsuitable FreeBSD/schema contract.
For feasible cases implement missing validation or adapters and demonstrate real startup/traffic where the source contract requires it.
Document intentional strict-section, IPv6-ignore, ECN-default, literal-prefix and upstream-layout differences without silently changing Linux defaults just to satisfy F-Stack assertions.

groups.title: Decide F-Stack primary/secondary and thread-mode compatibility
groups.reason: Explicit main/aux secondary EAL requests now fail preflight before worker execution; a live same-prefix primary survives and completes real native TCP/UDP. Actual isolated auto-primary and CLI primary overriding INI secondary are qualified extensions. The six pinned cases instead require secondary acceptance/proc_id tables and valid thread_mode multi-stack/global process-count semantics, which remain absent. Four local RX pollers or independent primaries are not those contracts.
acceptance: Specify whether shared/secondary worker behavior fits Ker, with explicit kernel-instance and device ownership.
Implement real mode selection, CLI precedence, lcore/index checks and rejection/unwind for unsupported combinations, or document the incompatible source contracts.
Do not relabel multiple independent native instances as F-Stack secondary processes.

groups.title: Document and qualify host/native stack coexistence configuration
groups.reason: Actual Ker descriptor-based coexistence now has real host/native identical-UDP-tuple traffic, mixed epoll full64-bit tags, independent close orders and exact native-only UDP counters. The four pinned assertions instead inspect a F-Stack global boolean:1/0/garbage supplied sections are explicitly rejected by Ker, while section absence keeps coexistence active without a synthetic default field. These source configuration contracts remain blocked, not runtime passes.
acceptance: Record the supported Ker coexistence contract and whether a global mode flag is needed.
Retain real host/native same-number descriptor and independent-traffic evidence; do not infer equivalence to F-Stack boolean parsing.
Add any useful configuration behavior and rejection tests, or document why the original flag/default assertions are not portable.

groups.title: Resolve unmapped host memory, time, environment and kqueue helpers
groups.reason: Three allocation scenarios now have actual native-buffer-domain acceptance: zero-initialized allocation, prefix-preserving resize and zero-size pointer identity. Remaining F-Stack cached time/environment, fatal/shared/file mapping and host kqueue helper ABI cases need their actual adapter or explicit incompatibility disposition; no libc-only test or successful unsupported stub qualifies. The observable two-refresh advancing-realtime case now uses the production synchronization adapter and actual private Linux clock; the cached getter/nullable split-output and fatal refresh-error ABI cases remain incomplete.
acceptance: Determine an actual Ker/LKL consumer and contract for each helper, or record why the source-specific API is unsuitable.
Test a real production adapter if one is required, including allocation/error/null-output behavior and cleanup.
Do not add unused wrappers, libc-only smoke tests, successful unsupported stubs or a FreeBSD hardclock layer merely to reduce migration counts.

groups.title: Resolve FreeBSD thread context and join-result assertions
groups.reason: Exact source review identifies three F-Stack/FreeBSD-specific assertions: opaque pcurthread pointer inheritance, discarding a non-NULL start result through a join result slot absent from LKL, and a test-local FreeBSD PCPU_GET null-context panic mirror that never creates a thread. Preserve original Linux task/TLS and the pinned LKL void-start/handle-only-join ABI. These are explicitly excluded, not Ker passes; source IDs and executable alternative boundaries are documented.
acceptance: Retain each exact source assertion and pinned provenance; do not count Linux thread/TLS tests as these FreeBSD ABI passes.
Keep the real native-fstack-thread-runtime argument/allocation-failure adaptations and runtime extensions separately qualified.
Reopen adaptation only if an actual Ker consumer requires the source-specific ABI; do not synthesize FreeBSD task/PCPU pointers or alter upstream LKL callback signatures merely for a test.

groups.title: Record nonportable callout, kqueue, mbuf and page-array build assertions
groups.reason: These assertions depend on FreeBSD sbintime/hardclock/tick conversion, timer activation macros, internal kqueue filter IDs or mbuf M_PKTHDR/m_pkthdr.len fields. Original Linux has different timer/readiness/skb representations; a VMA payload or fabricated FreeBSD header mirror does not qualify them. The FF_USE_PAGE_ARRAY reload restriction depends on process-private FreeBSD bsd_m_table references, with a conditional reject/on and accept/off source pair; it is not a generic Linux allocator contract.
acceptance: Confirm each listed assertion is FreeBSD-internal and document the supported Linux timer/readiness behavior with existing runnable evidence.
Do not transplant FreeBSD internals or declare their tests passed on unrelated Linux behavior.
Retain pinned source provenance and an explicit architecture-specific disposition.

groups.title: Disposition upstream reload-tool self-tests and CMocka smoke cases
groups.reason: These entries test the F-Stack remote reload orchestration/capture tooling or CMocka itself. Executing copied harness tests would not demonstrate Ker networking, reload ownership or protocol compatibility.
acceptance: Keep all source cases discoverable and pinned without executing remote-host/process-control helpers implicitly.
Decide which orchestration helpers should be reworked for an implemented Ker reload runner; tie those adaptations to the reload issue and real acceptance evidence.
Explicitly record framework-only smoke exclusions without counting them as native network passes.
